title: US 194,047 (N. A. Otto, Improvement in Gas-Motor Engines, 14 Aug 1877): full patent PDF, 8 pages (pages 1-4 are drawing sheets 1-4, pages 5-8 the specification)
license_quote: Patent published 1877-08-14; Google Patents legal status "Expired - Lifetime". A US patent grant of 1877 is a pre-1929 government-published document.
credit: USPTO via Google Patents (N. A. Otto, 1877)
why: The Otto patent drawing the brief asks for. Sheet 2 (Fig. 2) is the full engine in side elevation with flywheel; sheet 1 Fig. 1 is the cylinder section; sheet 4 has valve-gear details. Opened and rendered in this session: pages 1-4 are drawings, 5-8 text. The drawing is a gas engine with a layered charge, not a modern-looking four-stroke: caption it "Otto, 1877 patent", and do not present it as the modern cycle.
resolution: PDF, 8 pages; rasterise pages 1-4 at 300 dpi in Actions

title: US 194,047, drawing sheet 4 (Figs. 6-13, valve gear details), full size PNG
credit: USPTO via Google Patents (N. A. Otto, 1877)
why: Direct PNG (2320 x 3408, 1-bit) opened in this session. Sheets 1-3 have no direct PNG link on the Google page: take them from P1.

title: TM 10-570, The Internal Combustion Engine (War Department Technical Manual, 4 Feb 1941), 4-stroke diagrams, valve timing figure 53, power-stroke overlap Figs. 15-17
license_quote: Internet Archive metadata licenseurl: http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark). Author: United States. War Department; publisher: U.S. G.P.O. (a US government publication). Commons has the same file tagged Public domain.
credit: U.S. War Department / U.S. Government Publishing Office (1941), via Internet Archive
why: The best US-government visual find: 1940s technical-manual line drawings of the four events (Fig. 4 intake onward), compression ratio (Fig. 7), the four-cylinder (Fig. 15) and six-cylinder (Fig. 16) power overlap charts and valve timing (Fig. 53, named in the text). The text of the same manual is cited in claims.json as TM 10-570. Figure numbers come from the OCR text: confirm each when rasterised. PDF headers returned 200 (34 MB).

title: Dugald Clerk, The Gas, Petrol and Oil Engine, vol. II: The Gas, Petrol and Oil Engine in Practice (Longmans, 1909), engravings and diagrams of Otto-cycle petrol motors, crankshaft and firing-order figures
license_quote: Cornell scan front page (read in the OCR text of this item): "There are no known copyright restrictions in the United States on the use of the text." Published 1909, before 1929, so public domain in the US. Commons file page tags it Public domain.
credit: Dugald Clerk and G. A. Burls, Longmans, Green and Co., 1909; scan by Cornell University Library via Internet Archive
why: Pre-1929 engravings and indicator diagrams of early petrol engines; firing-order and crankshaft figures (fig. 295 and following, four-cylinder section; the text discusses figs. 300-303). Also the text source for claims 5.4, 7.1, 7.2 and 7.6. Figure pages not individually checked: find the Otto-engine and crankshaft plates by searching the OCR when fetched.

title: Alphonse Beau de Rochas (photograph of a painting), Commons File:Beauderochas.jpg
license_quote: Commons extmetadata: "Public domain" (transferred from en.wikipedia by User:Addhoc). Description: photograph of a painting of Alphonse Beau de Rochas.

why: Only portrait found. 180 x 248 px: too small for a full-frame shot; use as a small inset or redraw in 2D from it. The painting date and painter are not stated, so the PD tag rests on Commons only: weakest licence of the usable set. Do not use it if the fact check wants a stronger basis.

title: NASA Glenn: animated drawing of one cylinder of the Wright 1903 four-stroke engine (cylmov2.gif, 646 x 486, 3.1 MB) and its stroke stills engop1-4
license_quote: NASA Images and Media Usage Guidelines: "NASA content ... generally are not subject to copyright in the United States." Page notes NASA sometimes uses third-party copyrighted material and marks it with the holder's name; no third-party mark was seen on this page.
why: Reference only (low resolution, 1903 engine, NASA colour code differs from ours): useful to check our own Blender cutaway animation, not as a final shot. GIF downloaded and checked in this session.

title: Prelinger Archives: "Elements of the Automobile, Pt II: The Engine" (archive.org 0953_Elements_Of_The_Automobile_Pt_II_The_Engine)
license_quote: Metadata has no licenseurl, no producer/sponsor, no date and no rights field; the description is only "Examines the automobile engine."
why: Probably an old educational film, but the producer and date are not recorded: cannot call it a US government work or pre-1929. NOT usable until provenance is found.

title: US government engine footage (Army, Navy, NASA, NARA training films)
license_quote: Searched archive.org (movies, Prelinger, army collections) and Wikimedia Commons: no four-stroke explainer film with a verified US-government or pre-1929 origin was found.
why: Not found. The Army 1941 technical manual (D1) is the government visual we did verify. A NARA catalogue or Library of Congress search is the next place to look; it needs a session with those hosts allowed.
